$comment: A fixed corpus for the memory recall benchmark. Facts are what a person would actually /remember about a repository; queries name the fact they should bring back. kind=lexical shares a distinctive word with its fact on purpose (the local ranker's floor); kind=paraphrase and kind=crosslingual share no word with it, which is the case embedding recall exists for. docs/memory-bench.md explains the columns.

facts.value: run go test ./... -count=1 with HOME redirected under the sandbox
go test -race runs in the CI Build and Lint job
tag v0.x.y and push the tag; goreleaser is not used
Postgres at 10.4.2.11:5432, read-only for everyone
make migrate-up; never edit a migration that has been applied
production ships from the release branch, never a direct push to master
neovim with gopls; format on save is off
gopls comes from mise, not brew
the web app uses pnpm, never npm
tokens live in 1Password under gateway, never in .env
the seatbelt probe fails inside a nested sandbox; it is tracked, not broken
logs go to stderr; the file logger exists for the TUI only
the public API is versioned in the path (/v1), never by header
a cache hit is only counted when the prefix matches byte for byte
deepseek-flash is the default route; the older alias is retired
budgets are per run and per session; zero means unlimited
sessions are JSON files under ~/.tinycode/sessions, one per session
checkpoints keep pre-images, so undo restores bytes rather than applying a diff
writes are fenced to the project root unless a grant widens it
Windows is unsupported; the build assumes unix
CI runs nine jobs; annotations are not part of the pass criteria
documentation is English; the README is the entry point
errors wrap with %w and the message reads lowercase
memory facts are per project and live outside the repository
